directions.name: The Index Page
directions.concept: A flush-left masthead — name set very large and very tight, a two-line deck beneath it — sitting above a six-row typographic index ruled with true 1px hairlines. No tiles, no shadows, no motion beyond a 1px chevron that steps 3px right; the only color in the whole page is a single accent period after the name.
directions.rationale: The current page has no identity anchor, so the fix is not to decorate the icons — it is to make the name the largest object on the screen and demote the links to what they actually are: an index of six destinations. Setting them as a ruled list solves four of the listed problems at once: the flex-wrap 2+1 reflow disappears because it is a single column that cannot wrap; the six mismatched glyphs stop competing because they are reduced to a 14px optical box (±1px of deliberate per-mark correction) with one shared color; the drop-shadow goes; and every text pair is re-tuned to 6.77:1 or better. The mono annotation column ("code", "rides & runs", the actual email address) is where the person shows up — it tells you why you would click, in the voice of someone who writes software, and it pairs an editorial grotesque against a monospace the way a well-set spec sheet does. The accent finally does work: the period after the name, the hairline under a hovered row, the focus ring. Three uses, one hue, and now the purple favicon has a reason to exist.
directions.idealTypeface: What I actually want is Söhne (Klim) — Buch for the deck and index labels, Kräftig for the name. Its 1957-Helvetica skeleton with modern, tight display spacing is precisely the design-annual feel, and it takes -0.04em tracking at 96px without the caps colliding. The shippable, self-hostable substitute is Inter Tight Variable (OFL, one ~90KB Latin-subset woff2 covering 500–700) plus Commit Mono or JetBrains Mono for the metadata column. Either buys three concrete things system-ui cannot: (1) real small caps via `font-variant-caps: all-small-caps` for the six labels instead of the faux-uppercase-plus-0.115em-tracking I am forced into here; (2) a display-grade `A` with tight sidebearings so the name can be tracked to -0.042em and still breathe; (3) deterministic metrics — right now the same CSS gives you SF on macOS, Roboto on Android, Segoe on Windows, and the name's optical weight and rag change on each. Measured here on SF, "Ankur Gupta." sets 220.9px wide at 40px, leaving 103px of slack in the narrowest 380px panel — comfortable, but that slack is exactly what varies per platform, and it is the reason the full-scale ramp must be a clamp rather than a fixed size. Ship it with `size-adjust` on a system-ui fallback @font-face so there is zero layout shift.

directions.astroNotes:
Base.astro token surgery. Collapse --bg-1/--bg-2 into a single --paper (#f5f5f3 / #0e0e10) and delete the radial-gradient from `body` — `background: var(--paper)` only. The vignette is what makes the current page feel like a splash screen; flat ground is the whole premise here. Keep --fg but rename to --ink. Delete --muted outright and replace with --ink-soft #55555c / #9e9ea6 — every use site in this design measures 6.77:1 or better. (Verified the diagnosis: --muted #8a8a90 is 3.12:1 over --bg-1 #f4f4f5 and 2.51:1 over --bg-2 #dcdce0; dark --muted #6b6b72 is 3.41:1 over #16161a and 3.74:1 over #0a0a0c. All four fail 4.5:1.) Collapse --icon/--icon-hover into --ink-soft with hover promoting to --ink, so there is no separate icon color system. Retune --accent from #5b3df5 to #4b31d9 (light) / #a99bff (dark): same hue family as the favicon. Be precise about why — #5b3df5 measures 5.57:1 over the gradient's inner stop and 4.48:1 over its outer stop, so it passes AA at the page centre and fails only out at the vignette edge; flattening the ground is half the fix and the retune to 7.02:1 is the other half. Add --rule / --rule-strong, --sans, --mono. Also update public/favicon.svg's rect fill to #4b31d9 and set the `g` in the self-hosted face at the same -0.038em so the tab mark and the page are visibly the same object.

Box sizing is not optional here. Base.astro already ships `* { box-sizing: border-box }` — keep it. The measure is load-bearing: under content-box, `max-width: 34rem` caps the content box, so the real cap becomes 37.5rem (measured 560px instead of 544px in a 560px panel). The scoped preview CSS declares border-box explicitly for exactly that reason; in the real build the global reset covers it.

Fonts. Add /public/fonts/InterTight-var.woff2 (or Söhne if licensed) + one mono, `@font-face` with `font-display: swap`, `<link rel="preload" as="font" crossorigin>` in Base.astro's head, and a `@font-face { font-family: 'sans-fallback'; src: local('system-ui'); size-adjust: ~97% }` so the swap is metric-neutral. Then switch `.label` from `text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .115em` to `font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; letter-spacing: .085em` — real small caps, less tracking needed.

index.astro. The two `rows` arrays and .socials/.row/.social styles all go; iterate one flat `links` array into a single-column nav, which structurally eliminates the 2+1 flex-wrap reflow. Add a `note` field per link ('code', 'work', the email address, 'rides & runs', 'listening', 'settle up') and drop the `title` attributes entirely. Move the `<footer>` inside the same max-width column so the colophon aligns to the rules rather than centering. In the real page the header/footer belong at body level as the document's banner/contentinfo — the preview wraps them in `<article>` only because four panels on one comparison page would otherwise emit four competing banner landmarks. Replace the Venmo `<text>V</text>` placeholder with a real logo path: it renders as a visibly foreign Georgia italic inside the grotesque at every size, and it also leaks a stray "V" into the row's textContent (not into the accessible name — the span and svg are both aria-hidden, and the six computed link names check out as e.g. "GitHub code Opens in a new tab"). Still zero JS, still one stylesheet.

At true full-viewport scale. The composition stays flush-left, offset `padding-inline-start: clamp(1.5rem, 7vw, 6rem)`, content column `max-width: 46rem`, and the whole block vertically centered then nudged up ~4% so it sits above the optical center. Type ramp opens up: name `clamp(2.75rem, 9vw, 6rem)` with tracking tightening as it grows — -0.034em at the small end, -0.042em past 4.5rem (set via a single media query, not one static value); deck `clamp(1rem, 2.2vw, 1.1875rem)/1.5` with `max-width: 34ch` so it stays a two-line deck instead of stretching into a paragraph; label 0.875rem, note 0.75rem, colophon 0.75rem. Rows go to `padding: 1.125rem 0` (≈52–56px) for real touch targets — note the ≤430px branch here already lands at a measured 44.59px, so the mobile case is compliant before the desktop ramp ever applies. The annotation column gains `padding-left: 3rem`, which also buys back headroom before the ellipsis can engage. The one thing that must NOT scale: the hairlines stay exactly 1px and the opening rule stays exactly one step darker. At 6rem type, a 2px rule reads as a border and the page immediately looks like a UI instead of a page. Pin the colophon to the bottom edge with `margin-top: auto` once there is real height to spend.
risks: A type-only page is only as good as its typeface. On the system stack it renders as SF on macOS, Roboto on Android, Segoe on Windows — and -0.038em tracking that reads confident on SF reads cramped on Roboto. Without the self-hosted woff2 this direction is meaningfully worse, not slightly worse.

Uppercase labels plus a right-aligned monospace column plus hairline rules is one wrong step away from looking like a settings screen or an API reference table. The thing holding it on the right side of that line is the 40px name and the 221px of index sitting under a much larger void — if a future edit adds a seventh row or a second paragraph, it tips.

There is no warmth, no image, no color beyond a single period. Someone arriving expecting personality may read it as cold or unfinished in a different way than the current page is unfinished. This is a bet that confidence reads better than charm, and it is a bet.

Swiss-editorial-plus-mono-metadata is itself a strong 2020s portfolio idiom. It will age better than embossed glyphs, but in five years it may read as "that template every engineer-designer used," and the very restraint that makes it defensible also makes it unmemorable next to a direction with a real idea in it.

The annotation column is copy, and copy is a liability. "code", "settle up", "listening" are doing real work — if they drift toward cute or filler, that column becomes the weakest thing on the page and there is nowhere for the eye to go instead.

At 14px the icons stop being logos. Strava's chevron and the Venmo V are barely identifiable at that size, so the words carry 100% of the recognition load — anyone scanning for a familiar colored logo will find nothing to lock onto and may scan slower than they do on the current icon grid.

The annotation column has a finite, now-measured width budget: 178px of track at the 380px panel floor against 127px for the longest real string. That is 51px of slack, or roughly seven more monospace characters. A longer email address or a wordier note silently truncates with the ellipsis landing on the right — which on the Email row means losing the domain, the one part that matters. Anyone editing that copy needs to know the ceiling is about twenty characters, not that it is unbounded.
qaReport: A. SCOPING — clean, and audited mechanically rather than by eye. I rendered the panel in Chrome and walked the live CSSOM: 37 style rules reference the scope token, and the only two selectors that do not begin with it are the `:root[data-theme="dark"] SCOPE` and `:root[data-theme="light"] SCOPE` blocks the contract explicitly requires. No `:root`, `html`, `body`, or bare `*` selector anywhere. All custom properties are declared on `SCOPE` itself. There are zero `@keyframes` in this direction, so the cross-panel name-collision risk does not exist here. All four at-rule contexts parse and apply: top level, `(prefers-color-scheme: dark)`, `(max-width: 430px)`, `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. I also confirmed both theme overrides actually resolve, by stamping `data-theme` on the root and reading computed values back: light gives --paper #f5f5f3 / --accent #4b31d9, dark gives #0e0e10 / #a99bff, and removing the attribute falls back correctly.

B. CONTRAST — every pair passes, so no token needed changing. But three of the ratios the direction *reports* were wrong, and they were about to go to a client as fact. --ink was claimed at 16.9:1 light / 17.6:1 dark; actual is 16.53 / 17.51. --ink-soft dark was claimed 7.27:1; actual 7.25. --accent was claimed 6.97:1 / 7.76:1; actual 7.02 / 8.10. All corrected in the palette. Computed with the real sRGB relative-luminance formula, not eyeballed.

B. CONTRAST — the rationale's claim that the existing #5b3df5 "fails AA on paper at 4.4:1" is imprecise about which ground. Measured: 5.57:1 over the gradient's inner stop #f4f4f5 and 4.48:1 over its outer stop #dcdce0. So it passes AA at the page centre and fails only out at the vignette edge — which is a better argument than the original one, because it makes flattening the ground half the fix rather than incidental to it. Restated accurately in astroNotes; the retune to #4b31d9 (7.02:1 on flat paper) stands.

B. CONTRAST — verified the direction's core diagnosis of the live site rather than taking it on trust. --muted #8a8a90 is 3.12:1 over --bg-1 and 2.51:1 over --bg-2; dark --muted #6b6b72 is 3.41:1 and 3.74:1. All four fail 4.5:1. Retiring --muted is correct and the numbers are now in astroNotes.

B. CONTRAST — the hairlines are intentionally far below 3:1 and that is legitimate: --rule measures 1.33:1 light / 1.42:1 dark and --rule-strong 2.03:1 / 2.51:1, but they are decorative separators, and 1.4.11 governs components and state, not rules. What carries state is the chevron (6.77:1 / 7.25:1) and the hovered rule promoting to accent (7.02:1 / 8.10:1), both comfortably over 3:1. Noted in the palette roles so nobody 'fixes' the hairlines later and wrecks the whole premise.

C. UNITS AND RESOURCES — clean. No vh/vw/dvh/svh/vmin/vmax anywhere in the CSS (the vw values in astroNotes are prose describing the real full-viewport build, not emitted CSS). No @import, no @font-face, no url(), no external host, no <script>. No `title` attribute. No inline `style` attribute at all, not even a custom property. Icons are placeholders only — no raw SVG in the markup.

D. CORRECTNESS — fixed a real box-sizing dependency. `.page` combines `max-width: 34rem` with 1.75rem padding, and the assembly host is not guaranteed to reset box-sizing. I rendered the panel on a page with deliberately no reset: the column came out 560px wide in a 560px panel instead of 544px, because under content-box `max-width: 34rem` caps the *content* box and the effective cap becomes 37.5rem. On a wider host the column would keep growing to 600px. Added `box-sizing: border-box` for the scope root and every padded or bordered descendant, enumerated per element rather than via `*` (which the contract bans). Re-measured: computed boxSizing is border-box and the column is back to 544px.

D. CORRECTNESS — `::selection { background: ... }` changed to `background-color`. Only a restricted property set is honoured inside ::selection and the shorthand is not portable there. Confirmed `color-mix(in oklab, …)` is supported in the target engine so the accent token still resolves; the resulting selection composites to #d3ceee light / #2d2a40 dark, keeping ink on it at 11.89:1 / 12.57:1.

D. CORRECTNESS — `<div class="page">` became `<article class="page">`. A `<header>` and `<footer>` whose nearest ancestor is a plain div become document-scoped `banner` and `contentinfo` landmarks; on a shared four-panel comparison page that is four banners and four contentinfos fighting each other in the landmark list. `<article>` scopes them properly. Zero visual change, no class or CSS change, and astroNotes records that the real page wants them at body level instead.

D. CORRECTNESS — added missing focus parity. `.row:hover .ico` promoted the icon to --ink but the focus state did not, so a keyboard user got a strictly weaker treatment than a mouse user. Added `.row:focus-visible .ico`. Verified by focusing a row and reading settled values: chevron border goes to accent rgb(75,49,217), icon goes to ink rgb(22,22,26), and both return to --ink-soft on blur. Focus stays clearly distinct from hover — focus is outline plus accent chevron, hover is the accent rule plus the 3px step — and the chevron transform confirms the 3px translate is hover-only.

D. CORRECTNESS — hardened the icon transforms. The six per-mark optical scales all assume the SVG root scales about its own centre. An outermost `<svg>`'s `transform-origin` has a history of resolving to `0 0` rather than `50% 50%`, which would silently convert every one of those corrections into an off-centre nudge. Pinned `transform-box: border-box; transform-origin: 50% 50%`. Chrome already did the right thing — measured icon boxes are exactly 14 × scale (13.16, 12.60, 13.58, 15.96, 13.16, 14.84) — so this is a cross-engine guard, not a Chrome bug fix.

E. CRAFT — fixed the one real touch-target failure. Rows measured 36.7px at panel scale and 37.6px in the ≤430px branch: fine for WCAG 2.5.8 (24px) but under 2.5.5 (44px) on the single breakpoint that is actually a finger. Raised the narrow-branch row padding from 0.6875rem to 0.875rem and measured 44.59px. It costs nothing at panel scale because that media query cannot fire in a side-by-side grid on a wide screen, and the height is already paid for by hiding the annotation column there. Re-verified the whole narrow branch while I was in it: 3-column grid, note display:none, name at 34px fitting 190.3px into 340px, no horizontal burst.

E. CRAFT — the rhythm numbers in the header comment were estimates and slightly wrong. The index measures 221.17px (1px + 6 × 36.695), not 220.6, and the total is 431.7px, not 431. On a page whose entire argument is typographic precision, an off-by-half-a-pixel comment is the wrong signal. Replaced with browser-measured values. Confirmed the composition fits a 440px panel with about 8px of slack at 380, 470 and 560px, and that the deck holds at exactly two lines at all three widths as the direction claims.

E. CRAFT — added `white-space: nowrap` to `.site` and `.copy`. The colophon is a two-item space-between flex row with no wrap guard; at the narrow floor a wrapped copyright line would have broken the bottom of the rhythm. Measured at 13.2px single-line everywhere after the change.

F. RETRACTED FINDING — I want this on the record so nobody re-introduces it. I was confident `overflow: hidden` on `.note` made it baseline-opaque and therefore broke the row's `align-items: baseline`, and I removed the ellipsis guard on that basis. Then I measured it: I injected zero-size inline-block baseline probes into the label and the note in both the original and my edit, and the baseline delta is exactly 0.00px in both, with identical 36.695px row heights. Grid and flex items take their first formatted line's baseline per CSS Box Alignment; the overflow exception is specific to inline-block in inline layout and does not apply here. The author was right and I was wrong. Worse, removing the clip is an actual regression: with a long note the panel's scrollWidth blew out to 473px inside a 380px panel. Fully reverted to the author's `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`, and the comment now quantifies the real headroom instead of asserting a phantom bug.

G. CHECKED, DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED — the index opens on --rule-strong but closes on a light --rule. Editorial tables usually bracket top and bottom at equal weight, so this reads at first like an oversight, but the token's stated role is specifically 'the opening rule' and an open-ended bottom edge is a coherent choice for something called an index. Not my call to overturn; flagging it as a one-line change if the client wants the block closed.

G. CHECKED, DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED — Strava's 1.14 scale renders 15.96px inside a nominal 14px column, so that one mark overhangs the flush-left rule edge by about 1px. That is correct optical practice for a thin chevron and it is precisely what makes the six glyphs read at a single weight, which is the direction's stated goal. Measured and accepted rather than 'corrected' into a visible weight mismatch.

G. CHECKED, DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED — `.row`, `.mark` and `.ico` transition color and border-color, which are also theme-token-driven, so on a `data-theme` flip the six hairlines and six icons cross-fade over 140ms while every other token snaps. I caught this as a false positive first (a mid-transition computed read looked like the dark theme failing to apply to `.ico`) and confirmed it settles correctly after 400ms. Killing the transitions would remove the hover craft the direction is explicitly built around, for a 140ms shimmer during a deliberate user-initiated toggle. Documented, not changed.

G. CHECKED, DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED — `max-content` on the label track sizes independently per row, because each `.row` is its own grid container, so the six label tracks are genuinely different widths (47.5px to 73.1px). This has no visual consequence: the next track is `minmax(0, 1fr)` and the note is right-aligned, so icons, labels, notes and chevrons all measured flush across the six rows. Fragile only if someone ever left-aligns the annotation column.

G. VERIFIED, NO CHANGE NEEDED — all six hrefs match the live index.astro exactly. All five external links carry both `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; the mailto correctly carries neither. Every link has a real visible text label so none needs an aria-label. `:focus-visible` is present, matches on programmatic focus, renders a 2px solid accent outline at 3px offset, and sits 23px inside the panel edge on both sides so it cannot clip. Motion is confined to the chevron and is fully neutralised in `prefers-reduced-motion`, including the translate. No transition on `all`. No animation gates content visibility, so nothing disappears if motion never runs. Every class in the markup has a matching rule and no rule targets a class that does not exist.

G. VERIFIED — the production Venmo icon is `<text>V</text>` set in Georgia italic, and it renders in the screenshot as an unmistakably foreign serif inside a grotesque page. It also leaks a stray 'V' into the row's textContent, though not into the accessible name (both the wrapping span and the svg are aria-hidden, and the computed link names come out clean as e.g. 'GitHub code Opens in a new tab'). The direction already calls for replacing it; I confirmed it is a genuine problem rather than a theoretical one, and left the fix in astroNotes where it belongs.

directions.name: Structural Grid
directions.concept: A hard 1px grid divides the page into an explicit, deliberately uneven set of cells: the name owns the biggest one, each link owns its own numbered one, and a full-height saturated violet spine runs corner to corner down the right edge carrying the "g" from the favicon. The structure is the only ornament — no radius, no shadow, no movement.
directions.rationale: Six links is a catalogue, not a constellation, so I set it as one: an index with ordinals 01–06, column one professional (GitHub, LinkedIn, Email), column two personal (Strava, Spotify, Venmo), grouping carried by adjacency and numbering instead of extra chrome. That fixes the listed problems structurally rather than cosmetically — an explicit grid cannot reflow raggedly the way two flex-wrap rows do; every mark sits in a fixed 20px box at a per-glyph optical size, with a text label doing the identifying, so GitHub's filled circle no longer outweighs Strava's hairline chevron; the drop-shadow is gone because a flat system has nothing to emboss. The name finally exists, set at 48px heavy caps flush to the bottom-left of the largest cell, with the violet spine's "g" at the top-right — one diagonal holding the whole composition together. The accent is used exactly twice and both times decisively: it permanently fills the spine top to bottom, and it fills an entire cell on focus. That is what finally earns the purple favicon a relationship to the site. Hover is the literal brief: ground and ink swap across a whole cell, zero movement, 80ms linear so it reads as a snap rather than a fade. For a software engineer who also races bikes and listens hard, a rigorous grid with mono metadata reads as someone who builds things precisely; the tagline plus the Strava and Spotify cells carry the rest without a paragraph of prose.
directions.idealTypeface: ABC Diatype for the name and labels, ABC Diatype Mono for every metadata line. Diatype is a low-contrast, slightly mechanical grotesque with tight apertures and a flat-sided "g" — it holds up at 48px heavy caps with -0.03em tracking without the humanist softness system-ui brings, and because it ships a true monospaced companion built on the same skeleton, the display type and the mono metadata read as one voice rather than two fonts stapled together. That matters more here than in most directions: the entire typographic system is caps display against tracked mono, so the relationship between those two IS the typography. It also closes the one remaining hole in the icon set — the Venmo "V" is drawn as live text, so once Diatype is self-hosted the V is literally the same letterform as the name, not an approximation of it. Self-hostable as woff2 (commercial licence). Free alternates that keep the character: Space Grotesk + Departure Mono, or a Neue Haas Grotesk Display clone + JetBrains Mono. Two weights only (Regular, ExtraBold) plus one mono Regular — under 60KB subset to Latin.

directions.astroNotes:
BASE.ASTRO TOKENS. Replace the :root block wholesale with the eight tokens above and delete --bg-1, --bg-2, --fg, --muted, --icon, --icon-hover. Three of those are current bugs: --muted (#8a8a90 light / #6b6b72 dark) fails AA in both themes and is superseded by --ink-2 (8.00:1 / 8.16:1) and --ink-3 (5.75:1 / 5.93:1); --icon/--icon-hover become unnecessary because cells own their colour and SVGs inherit through fill: currentColor. Keep `color-scheme: light dark`. The body radial-gradient goes away — this direction needs a flat ground for the hairlines to read as drawn rules rather than sitting on a vignette; set `background: var(--ground)`. Keep the existing `* { box-sizing: border-box }`; my CSS re-declares box-sizing per element only because the preview contract forbids a universal selector, and those lines can be dropped in the real build.

INDEX.ASTRO. The `links` object stays, but flatten `rows` into a single ordered array [github, linkedin, email, strava, spotify, venmo] — `grid-auto-flow: column` turns that order into column one = work, column two = personal, so DOM order, visual reading order and tab order all agree without any `order` hacks (verified: tab lands 01, 02, 03, then 04, 05, 06). Three deletions from the current file: the `title={link.label}` attribute (native tooltip, slow and unstyleable — the visible label replaces it), the `filter: drop-shadow(...)`, and the per-anchor aria-label (now redundant, since the visible text label is the better accessible name — names come out as exactly "GITHUB", "LINKEDIN", … with no ordinal or stray glyph text). Add an index in the map for the ordinal: `{String(i + 1).padStart(2, '0')}`. Wrap `<Fragment set:html={link.svg} />` in `<span class="glyph" aria-hidden="true">` — this one is load-bearing, because the Venmo asset is an SVG `<text>` node whose "V" would otherwise leak into the accessible name; aria-hidden is what stops it. Footer year becomes `{new Date().getFullYear()}` inside the `.year` span.

VENMO ASSET. The `SCOPE .c-venmo .glyph svg text` rule is a real fix, not a hack: the asset sets font-family / font-style / font-weight as SVG *presentation attributes*, which sit below author CSS in the cascade, so the rule wins and the Georgia bold-italic V renders in the display face at ExtraBold (confirmed in-browser: computed font-family ui-sans-serif, style normal, weight 800). It is a stopgap, though — it depends on that `<text>` node existing. The real build should replace the asset with the Venmo wordmark glyph as a path, or with a V drawn in Diatype; when it does, this rule harmlessly stops matching and can be deleted.

FAVICON. Currently an `rx="14"` violet tile with a white "g" — in this system that rounded corner is the one element contradicting the design. Drop rx so it is a hard square, keep #5b3df5 and the white g, and it becomes literally the same object as the spine cell. That is what actually gives the purple favicon a relationship to the page.

GRID STRUCTURE. The rule system is `gap: 1px` plus `background: var(--rule)` on the grid plus a matching 1px border — this guarantees no doubled and no missing hairlines regardless of how cells span, which per-cell borders cannot. The nav is a real `<nav>` grid item (never `display: contents`, which drops the landmark role in some AT) carrying its own `1.18fr 1fr / repeat(3, 1fr)` and the same 1px gap. Note that `nv` occupies only column one, so the nav's internal divider is intentionally its own axis and does NOT align with the parent's column divider (that one is the spine edge) — the off-grid divider at ~54% is the point. Do not reach for `grid-template-columns: subgrid` here; there is nothing to inherit.

AT TRUE FULL-VIEWPORT SCALE. The frame should go full-bleed, inset by `clamp(0.75rem, 2vw, 2rem)`, so the rules span the whole screen — that is the most confident reading of this direction. Because the type ramp is keyed to `cqi` (container inline size) rather than vw, it already tracks the frame rather than the viewport, so an inset or max-widthed frame stays correct; just widen the clamp to `clamp(3rem, 11cqi, 8rem)` for the name. Then: spine 4.5rem → 6rem with the glyph at 4rem; link rows to about 5.5rem so the cells breathe; label 0.6875rem → 0.8125rem, ordinal and metadata 0.625rem → 0.6875rem; cell padding to 1rem 1.5rem. The 1px rules stay exactly 1px at every size — never scale them, that is the whole discipline of the style. Row one taking 1.05fr means the identity cell absorbs most of the extra height on a tall screen, which is the right poster behaviour: the name sits flush bottom-left beneath a large deliberate void with the "g" occupying its top-right corner. The spine now spans all four rows, so at page scale it runs the full height of the frame and the footer sits to its left in column one; keep it that way — the corner-to-corner bar is what makes it an anchor rather than a bookmark. On very wide screens cap the frame around 72rem centred, otherwise the two link columns get uncomfortably long relative to their 20px glyphs. Also raise the `@container (max-width: 27rem)` breakpoint if the real page ever renders the frame narrower than the preview panel; the tagline is stacked below it and side-by-side with the slash above it, and both states are correct — there is no width at which the two phrases sit on one line without the slash.
risks: The Venmo mark is still the weakest element, even after the CSS normalisation. The asset is an SVG <text> node, so the V is now whatever grotesque the OS resolves from the sans stack rather than a drawn glyph - it will differ slightly between macOS, Windows and Android, and it is the one mark in the set whose weight I cannot tune independently of its width. It needs replacing with a real path before launch; the CSS rule is a stopgap that stops it looking like a mistake, not a finished mark.

Neo-brutalism is a datable style. Hard 1px rules plus one saturated violet reads distinctly 2022-2026 and will age faster than a quieter typographic direction. The composition underneath (asymmetric grid, uneven row rhythm, mono metadata) would survive a retune of the accent, but the surface will not stay current for a decade.

The design leans hard on the purple - the spine is now roughly 17% of the panel, and running it corner to corner made it more dominant, not less. This is deliberate, since it is the fix for an unused --accent and an unrelated favicon, but it is not a sprinkle that can be quietly removed. If Ankur does not love #5b3df5, this direction has to be re-pitched around a different colour rather than toned down.

Lifting the dark --rule from #48484f to #62626b was required to clear 3:1, and it does make the dark theme read a little more like a wireframe than the near-invisible original did. That is the correct trade for a direction whose entire ornament is the hairline, but it is a visible change in character between the two themes: light reads as ink on paper, dark reads as drawn structure.

The all-caps name uses text-transform so the DOM keeps 'Ankur Gupta', but Chrome exposes the transformed string to the accessibility tree and some screen readers spell short all-caps words letter by letter. Most AT reads the raw text and is fine; it is a small, real, unfixable-in-CSS wart.

Hover inverting to near-white in dark mode is a large luminance jump - a bright block flashing on a dark screen on every pointer pass. It is the correct literal inversion and it looks strong, but some users will find repeated full-cell inversion harsh at night. Softening it to a light grey instead of full --ink would blunt the idea; I chose the idea.

On focus the ordinal goes full white along with the label, so the 01-06 tier momentarily collapses into the rest of the cell. I considered a translucent white to preserve the tier and rejected it: 'the accent claims the entire cell' is the stated behaviour and a half-tone number reads as an accident on a flat fill.

The compact layout is driven by @container, so if the host ever wraps SCOPE such that inline-size containment does not apply, that breakpoint silently never fires - and with it the tagline stays a wrapping row rather than a stack. The base sizes do fit 380px so nothing breaks or clips, but the cells get tight rather than adapting.

Six equal peer cells can still read as a plain table to some eyes despite the off-centre 1.18fr divider and the ordinals. Someone with a stronger product opinion may want Email promoted to a wide cell; I judged that the wrong trade, since it forces the remaining five to tile awkwardly and hands Venmo a position of hierarchy it has not earned.

The metadata tier is 10px mono. It passes contrast comfortably at 5.75:1 and up, but it is at the small end of comfortable and is the first thing that will feel cramped for anyone who zooms or reads at arm's length.
qaReport: A. SCOPING - clean, nothing to fix. Parsed all 52 selectors mechanically: every one begins with the literal SCOPE token, apart from the two contract-mandated theme overrides (`:root[data-theme="dark"] SCOPE`, `:root[data-theme="light"] SCOPE`). No :root / html / body / bare-* selectors, no bare element or class selectors. All eight custom properties plus --sans/--mono are declared on SCOPE itself. There are no @keyframes at all, so no cross-direction name collision is possible. Both theme override blocks are present and correctly formed, and both outrank the prefers-color-scheme block on specificity (0,3,0 vs 0,1,0), so the host's data-theme toggle wins in both directions.

B. CONTRAST - one real failure found and fixed, in the non-text tier. Computed every pair with the WCAG relative-luminance formula (see contrastChecks). Every text pair passes, and the author's stated ratios were all accurate to two decimals - including the --ink-3-inv justification, which I verified lands at exactly 3.00:1 light / 2.88:1 dark without the token. THE FAILURE: dark --rule #48484f is 2.13:1 against #0e0e11. Those 1px lines are the boundaries that delimit six interactive cells, so they are held to 3:1 under 1.4.11, and in a browser render at 380-560px they were effectively invisible - which kills the direction's own thesis that the structure is the only ornament. Raised to #62626b for 3.19:1, confirmed in-browser. Kept light #222226 (14.41:1) untouched. Side effect accepted: the raised rule is only 1.16:1 against the violet, so the hairline disappears where it borders the spine - fine, because the spine's edge is already defined by the violet/ground boundary itself.

C. UNITS AND RESOURCES - clean, nothing to fix. Grepped for vh/vw/dvh/svh: zero hits. The `10cqi` in the name clamp is a container query unit, not a viewport unit, and it is legal here: container-type: inline-size is declared on SCOPE, and the preceding `font-size: 2.75rem` is a correct fallback for engines that drop the cq-unit declaration. No url(), no http(s) reference, no @font-face, no <script>, no title attribute anywhere in the HTML, no inline style attributes at all (not even custom-property ones - nothing is staggered), no !important.

D1. CORRECTNESS - the tagline collapsed into one unbroken line at ~440-460px wide. The narrow container query hid `.role .sep` while the two phrases still fitted side by side, so the panel rendered 'SOFTWARE & AI ENGINEERING RUNS, RIDES, LISTENS' as one nonsense string. Reproduced in Chrome at 440x440. Fixed by making the narrow state deterministic instead of hiding a mark and hoping: `.role` becomes flex-direction: column with align-items: flex-start and row-gap 0.25rem below 27rem, and only then is the slash dropped. Verified: 380 and 440 stack cleanly on two lines; 470 and 560 sit on one line with the slash. There is now no width at which the two phrases butt together unmarked.

D2. CORRECTNESS - the spine was described as full-height in the concept but was not built that way: `grid-template-areas` ran the footer as `"mt mt"` across both columns, so the violet stopped short of the bottom-right corner. Changed to `"mt mk"`. Verified in-browser: the mark's bottom is now 1px from the frame's inner edge, i.e. corner to corner, with the footer as a cell in column one. This is the one composition change I made, and I made it because the written intent was unambiguous ('a full-height saturated violet spine anchors the right edge') and the build contradicted it. It also reads better: an anchor rather than a bookmark.

D3. CORRECTNESS - `.mark` declared `grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto` but contains only two children, so the third track was dead and the wordmark was actually landing in the 1fr track. It rendered correctly only by accident (vertical-rl plus rotate(180deg) puts the text at the visual bottom of the stretched box). Replaced with an honest `auto 1fr`: byte-identical rendering, one phantom track gone. Also added `overflow: hidden` to `.mark` so the vertical wordmark can never spill across a hairline on a shorter host.

D4. CORRECTNESS - the direction's own #1 stated risk, the Georgia bold-italic Venmo V, turned out to be fixable in CSS without writing any SVG. The asset sets font-family / font-style / font-weight as SVG presentation attributes, and presentation attributes lose to any author rule, so `SCOPE .c-venmo .glyph svg text { font-family: var(--sans); font-style: normal; font-weight: 800 }` pulls it into the display face. Verified by computed style (ui-sans-serif / normal / 800 / 23px) and by eye in both themes: the V now reads as a member of the set instead of the one serif in the room. I deliberately did NOT touch its font-size, so the asset's own metrics and centring are preserved. Left the asset-replacement note in astroNotes and rewrote the risk accordingly - this is a stopgap, not a resolution.

D5. CORRECTNESS - everything else in this category checks out. All six hrefs match the brief; target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" on all five external links and on neither attribute of the mailto (verified by parsing every anchor). Real <h1> for the name, real <nav aria-label="Profiles and contact">. No icon-only links, so no aria-label is needed - each anchor's accessible name comes from its visible label, with the glyph and the ordinal both aria-hidden. Every class in the HTML is styled and every selector in the CSS matches something. :focus-visible is present and distinct from hover; I confirmed in Chrome that a focused cell computes to background rgb(106,76,251), color white, and a white 2px outline at -6px, and that focus-visible correctly beats hover on source order at equal specificity. The transition names two properties, never `all`. There is no animation or transform at all, so the prefers-reduced-motion block cannot be hiding content that fails to appear.

E1. CRAFT - hardened the two places where text could clip without a fallback. `.label` is white-space: nowrap inside a cell with overflow: hidden, so it could be sliced mid-word on a very narrow host; added min-width: 0, overflow: hidden and text-overflow: ellipsis so it degrades to an ellipsis instead. Added overflow: hidden to `.name` and `.meta` for the same reason - in a grid this rigid, any bleed across a hairline reads as a broken build. Added flex: 0 0 auto to `.meta .year` so the year can never be the thing that compresses.

E2. CRAFT - extended the forced-colors block. In Windows High Contrast every background-color is forced, which means the `gap: 1px` over `background: var(--rule)` technique loses all of its hairlines and the frame's border with them - a direction whose only ornament is structure would render as unstyled blocks. Added `border: 1px solid CanvasText` on the five cell-level elements plus `border-color: CanvasText` on the frame, so the grid survives. No layout shift: every box is border-box inside fixed tracks.

E3. CRAFT - removed `text-rendering: optimizeLegibility` from SCOPE. It is a known performance footgun in Blink and buys nothing here; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased is doing the real work and stays.

E4. CRAFT - things I checked and deliberately left alone. The 0.085em tracking on `.role` versus 0.1em everywhere else in the 10px mono tier looks like an inconsistency but is load-bearing: unifying it to 0.1em pushes the tagline about 4px wider and tips the 470px panel from one line into a wrap, so it is a deliberate fit, not a magic number. The 1.05fr on row one is documented in astroNotes as intentional. Icon marks are optically centred in a fixed 20px box rather than left-aligned, which keeps all six labels on one vertical axis - the right call for an index. The focus ring at outline-offset: -6px clears the glyph by 5px at the narrow cell padding, confirmed visually. Row-height arithmetic holds at the 25rem min-height floor: both flexible rows stay above their minmax minimums with no overflow.

E5. VERIFICATION - rendered the corrected panel in Chrome at 380x440, 440x440, 470x440, 560x440, 380x400 and 560x620, in both light and dark, plus a real keyboard-focused cell, and read computed styles back to confirm each fix landed (rule token, spine span, mark tracks, Venmo font, role direction and separator state at both sides of the breakpoint, label ellipsis). No horizontal overflow, no clipped type, no wrapped label, no ragged reflow at any of those sizes.

directions.name: Prompt Line
directions.concept: A single shell transcript: a prompt, the name run as the command, its two lines of output, a six-entry listing on a strict monospace grid, and an idle prompt with a blinking block caret. No window chrome, no ASCII art, no fake commands — the terminal reading comes entirely from the type, the grid, and one phosphor accent.
directions.rationale: The job is six links plus an identity anchor, which is exactly the shape of one `ls` invocation — so the metaphor is load-bearing rather than decorative, and it stops naturally at six rows without needing filler. It also solves the brief's hardest problem structurally: the six marks have wildly different optical mass, and dropping each into a fixed character cell beside a text label means the label carries recognition while the glyph only has to carry texture. Within any given width the `%`, the icon rail, the tagline and the caret all land on one identical x — measured at 52px in the narrow band and 60px at 440px, moving only when the inset token itself moves — which is the kind of rigor an engineer reads as competence rather than styling. And it earns the favicon back: #5b3df5 is literally the source of the accent, lifted to #a78bff only because the raw purple is 3.21:1 on near-black and cannot legally be text.
directions.idealTypeface: Berkeley Mono, self-hosted as a subset woff2. It buys three things this design leans on directly: a real Semibold instead of a synthesized 600, so the name can sit at display size without the fake-bold smearing Menlo and Liberation Mono produce; squarer counters and a slightly narrower advance, letting the label and path columns sit closer without mono's usual gappy rhythm at 14px; and a properly weighted %, ~, and › — all three are doing structural work here as the prompt and the selection marker, and they look weak in most system monos. Free self-hostable alternative: Commit Mono (variable, genuinely well drawn, and its optical-size handling survives the 13px-to-display jump). Avoid JetBrains Mono — the ligatures and mannered `l` fight the restraint. Note that the label column is sized in `ch`, so it self-corrects to whatever advance width the shipped face has — swapping the typeface will not desync the grid.
directions.proposedTagline: software & AI engineering. / long rides, long runs, loud music. — set as two deliberate output lines (line 1 "software & AI engineering", line 2 "long rides, long runs, loud music") rather than one sentence that wraps raggedly. Swap either line independently; keep each under ~33 characters so neither ever wraps (line 2 is currently 33 and was measured wrap-free down to 320px).

directions.astroNotes:
MAPPING ONTO Base.astro

This direction commits to one look, so the light/dark split collapses. Replace the `:root` block and DELETE the `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` override entirely:

  :root { color-scheme: dark;   /* was: light dark */
    --ground-a:#14141d; --ground-b:#0b0b11; --ground-c:#07070b;
    --ink:#eceaf4; --ink-2:#9a97a8; --ink-3:#8c8a99;
    --phos:#a78bff; --phos-2:#9880ea;
    --rule:rgba(167,139,255,.22); --sel:rgba(122,92,255,.15);
    --sel-active:rgba(122,92,255,.24); }

Token by token against what is there now:
- `--bg-1/--bg-2` (two stops) become `--ground-a/b/c` (three). The current `radial-gradient(130% 130% at 50% 35%, ...)` is centred and symmetrical; swap for `radial-gradient(115% 85% at 20% -5%, ...)` so the ground has a direction instead of a halo.
- `--fg #f0f0f2` -> `--ink #eceaf4`, slightly violet-warm so it does not read cold against the accent.
- `--muted` is DELETED. It is the token that fails AA in both themes (3.42:1 dark / 3.12:1 light), and it fails because one token was doing two jobs. It splits into `--ink-2` (6.1:1 worst case) and `--ink-3` (5.2:1, the year and nothing else). Nothing on the page is below 4.66:1.
- `--icon` / `--icon-hover` are gone. Marks take `--ink-2` at rest and `--phos` when lit: they are ink, not a parallel system.
- `--accent: #5b3df5` finally does something, but indirectly. It is 3.21:1 on this ground and cannot legally be text, so keep it as `--accent-raw` for the favicon and derive `--phos: #a78bff` (6.5:1, hue 254 vs 250 - same family) as the usable value. Favicon and site are now provably one colour idea.
- `body { font-family: system-ui, ... }` -> the mono stack, with `@font-face` for the self-hosted woff2 ahead of it and `font-display: swap`.
- `body { min-height: 100dvh }` stays. Keep the flex column but do NOT add `justify-content: center` — see the centring note below. Move `container-type: inline-size` and the grain `body::before` onto body, and keep the grain at opacity .03.

THREE IMPLEMENTATION TRAPS THIS VERSION FIXES — DO NOT REINTRODUCE THEM

1. Container queries cannot restyle their own container. The grid metrics
   (`--px`, `--gutter`, `--iconcol`, `--cg`, `--lbcol`) MUST be declared on `.term`,
   not on the element carrying `container-type`. Declared on the container they are
   silently unreachable from every `@container` block: the type shrinks at the
   breakpoint and the insets do not, which is a half-applied breakpoint that is very
   easy to miss. On the real page the same trap applies if `container-type` goes on
   `body` and the tokens live on `:root`. Either keep the tokens on `.term`, or use
   plain `@media` there (the viewport IS the measure once it is a full page).
2. `--lbcol: 8.5ch` resolves against the font-size of the element that USES it, so
   `.row` carries `font-size`, and `.lb`/`.hd` inherit it. Put the font-size back on
   `.lb`/`.hd` and the `ch` silently resolves at the inherited 16px instead of 14px,
   making the label column ~15px too wide and, worse, growing the label-to-path gap
   at exactly the breakpoint where space is scarcest. The breakpoints now change only
   `.row`'s font-size and the column follows.
3. Vertical centring is `margin-block: auto` on `.term`, NOT `justify-content: center`
   on the flex parent. Flex centring distributes negative free space in both
   directions, so as soon as content is taller than the box the top is clipped and is
   unreachable — the name loses its ascenders and no amount of scrolling recovers it.
   Auto margins resolve to 0 when free space is negative, so overflow only ever grows
   downward. This matters on the real page too: landscape phones and short windows.

MAPPING ONTO index.astro

- Each `links` entry gains `handle` (`/goobta`, `/in/goobta`, `rukna1000@gmail.com`, `/athletes/115751174`, `/user/theultimatepanda`, `/u/agupta628`) and `aria` (`"GitHub, github.com/goobta"` etc). Drop `title` entirely - the native tooltip is slow, unstyleable, and redundant beside a visible label. Keep the visible label text inside the aria string so WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name holds (verified for all six).
- `const rows = [[...],[...]]` is deleted. One flat array in the given order, rendered as six `<a>` inside one `<nav>`. This is what fixes the 3+3 -> 2+1 reflow bug: there is no `flex-wrap` anywhere, so there is nothing left to reflow.
- Delete `filter: drop-shadow(0 2px 2px ...)`. Flat monochrome glyphs have no light source to cast from; that is exactly why it reads embossed.
- Delete `transform: translateY(-3px)` on hover. Rows change colour and gain a surface; they do not move.
- The per-row class (`r-github` ... `r-venmo`) carries the optical scale correction, so no inline styles are needed anywhere.
- The Venmo mark in the current file is a serif italic "V" drawn with `<text>`, not a real logo. It reads visibly foreign beside five solid brand glyphs and its weight depends on a font the SVG does not control. Replace it with a real path before launch; the 1rem up-scale here is compensating for a placeholder.
- Footer year stays dynamic: `(c) {new Date().getFullYear()}`.

WHAT CHANGES AT TRUE FULL-VIEWPORT SCALE

Same layout, wider ramp - not a different design. Measured panel height is 393.5px at 440px wide, so there is real headroom to grow into.
- Name 1.375rem -> `clamp(2rem, 5.5vw, 3.25rem)`, tracking tightening from -0.028em to -0.038em above ~2.5rem. Line-height stays 1.1.
- Prompt sigil 0.8125rem -> `clamp(0.875rem, 1.6vw, 1.125rem)`. It must stay clearly subordinate; do not scale it 1:1 with the name. Whatever it grows to, the gutter must stay wider than the sigil's measure — it has ~2.5px of clearance at panel scale and that is the tightest tolerance in the layout.

risks: Terminal-as-personal-site is a well-worn engineer trope, and the only thing separating this from cosplay is what it refuses to do. It has almost no tolerance for accretion: add ASCII art, a typing animation, a scanline overlay, a fake `whoami`, or a second invented command and it collapses into a theme. Whoever maintains it has to understand that the restraint IS the design.

It commits to dark with no light fallback, by choice. A recruiter opening it on a phone in daylight gets a low-luminance page, and a light-mode user gets a page that ignores them. If that turns out to matter it cannot be patched with a token swap - the phosphor accent, the selection bar, and the grain are all derived from the near-black ground and would need re-deriving.

The violet phosphor is defensible today only because it reconciles the favicon. Change that icon and the accent becomes arbitrary. Violet-on-black also reads faintly 'AI startup' in 2026 in a way green or amber would not, which cuts against the timelessness the restraint is buying.

Monospace at 13-14px is genuinely less legible than a good sans at the same size - narrower apertures, more uniform word shapes - and it penalises low-vision readers more than a proportional face would, even though every pair here clears 4.5:1. The 19-character email address is where that is most exposed.

The path column is charming to engineers and opaque to everyone else. `/athletes/115751174` communicates literally nothing to a human reader, and `/user/theultimatepanda` front-loads mechanism over meaning. A words-based third column ('code', 'rides', 'listening') would be warmer but cutesier; I chose honesty and it costs some warmth.

It depends on the mono actually being good. Falling back to Liberation Mono on Linux, the -0.028em tracking on the name gets crowded, the marker glyph goes thin and weedy, and synthesized bold smears the display line. The self-hosted woff2 is not a nicety here, it is load-bearing.

Six single-line rows in a tight measure is a very fixed layout. A seventh link or a longer label is fine, but a whole new section (writing, projects) has nowhere to go without a second listing and a second prompt - at which point it starts to look like an actual shell session and reintroduces exactly the kitsch this version avoids.

The near-black ground plus a grain overlay leaves very little contrast headroom, and the quiet end of the ink ramp now sits at 5.2:1 with the ramp compressed (6.1 / 5.2 for the two muted levels). Any future darkening of the accent, any bump to the grain opacity, or any fourth ink level will push something under 4.5:1 — and it will do so invisibly, because the grain's effect on measured contrast is not something you can eyeball. Re-measure against --ground-a with the grain composited, not against a flat hex.

The layout's correctness rests on two non-obvious CSS facts (container queries cannot style their own container; `ch` resolves against the using element's font-size). Both are documented in comments, but a maintainer tidying the tokens back onto the container or the font-size back onto the labels will break the grid in a way that still looks plausible at desktop width.
qaReport: SCOPING — clean, no changes needed. Parsed every selector programmatically: all begin with the literal `SCOPE` token (the only non-SCOPE 'selectors' are the `0%/50%/100%` keyframe steps, which is correct). No `:root`, `html`, `body`, or `*`. All custom properties declared on `SCOPE` (colours) or `SCOPE .term` (grid metrics) — both scoped. The single `@keyframes` is `d2-caret`, correctly id-prefixed. `commitsToSingleTheme: true` with one token set on SCOPE, so the two theme-override blocks are legitimately absent per the contract.

CRITICAL / layout — `@container (max-width: 420px) { SCOPE { --px; --cg; --gutter } }` never applied. A container query cannot restyle its own container, and `SCOPE` carries `container-type: inline-size`. Measured: at 320px the row padding-left stayed 24px and `--px` stayed `1.5rem` while `.nm` correctly dropped to 19px and `.lb` to 13px — a silently half-applied breakpoint. FIXED by moving the five grid-metric tokens onto `SCOPE .term` (a descendant, so reachable) and overriding them there. Now measures 18px at ≤420px, 24px above.

CRITICAL / layout — content was clipped at the top and unrecoverable at ≤360px. `display:flex` + `justify-content:center` + `overflow:hidden` distributes negative free space in both directions: measured `.term` top offset of -33px at 320px and -22.9px at 360px, and the screenshot confirmed the name's ascenders sliced off with no way to scroll to them. FIXED by dropping `justify-content:center` and centring with `margin-block:auto` on `.term` — auto margins resolve to 0 when free space is negative, so overflow can only grow downward. Re-measured: top offset 0 at every width, name fully intact.

MAJOR / grid — `--lbcol: 8.5ch` resolved against the wrong font-size. `ch` computes on the element that uses it; `.row` inherited 16px from SCOPE while the labels rendered at 14px/13px. Measured label column of 81.875px at every width against a real need of ~67px, and the label-to-path gap grew to ~2.9 characters instead of the intended ~1.5 — worst at the narrow breakpoint where space is scarcest. FIXED by moving `font-size` onto `.row` and letting `.lb`/`.hd` inherit, so `ch` resolves at label size. Now 71.6px at 14px and 66.5px at 13px, with 4.17px / 3.89px clearance over 'linkedin' (~0.5ch as designed), and the breakpoints only need to change `.row`.

MAJOR / type — the tagline wrapped to three ragged lines at 320px ('long rides, long runs,' / 'loud music'), directly contradicting the direction's own promise that it never wraps. A downstream consequence of the container-query bug (the inset never shrank). FIXED by that repair plus stepping `.tag` to 0.75rem at ≤360px. Re-measured: exactly one line per span at all six test widths including 320px.

CONTRAST — two tokens failed 4.5:1 at their actual point of use, which the original numbers missed by measuring against bare `--ground-b`. I rasterised the exact `feTurbulence` data-URI and measured it: the noise has mean alpha 0.50 and mean channel ~186, so at `opacity: 0.05` it lifts `--ground-a`'s luminance from 0.00738 to 0.00964 (≈30% relative). Against that grained lightest stop, `--ink-3 #82808f` measured 4.37:1 and `--phos-2 #8a72e0` measured 4.48:1 — and `--phos-2` is the header prompt sigil, sitting exactly where the ground is lightest. FIXED three ways: grain 0.05 -> 0.03, `--ink-3` -> #8c8a99 (5.17:1), `--phos-2` -> #9880ea (5.50:1). Both stay clearly subordinate to their neighbours (6.13 and 6.47), so the ink ramp and the accent hierarchy are intact.

CRAFT — the prompt sigil was about to overflow its grid track. `~ %` measures 23.48px; the (previously dead) narrow-breakpoint rule shrank `--gutter` to 24px, leaving 0.52px of clearance — and fixing the container-query bug would have made that live, so any mono with a wider advance would break the spine. FIXED by holding `--gutter` at 1.625rem across both breakpoints and shrinking only `--px` and `--cg`. Measured 2.52px clearance at all six widths, and it keeps the spine metric stable.
CRAFT — removed `letter-spacing: 0.002em` on `.tag`: 0.026px at 13px, sub-pixel and visually inert. False precision in a design whose whole claim is exact metrics.

CRAFT — removed `text-rendering: optimizeLegibility`. It buys nothing for a monospace UI face and is a known source of inconsistent metrics across engines, which is a poor fit next to the -0.028em tracking on the display line.

CRAFT — raised `--rule` from 0.16 to 0.22 alpha. At 0.16 the hairlines composite to 1.24:1 against the ground; they carry the listing's entire structure and were at real risk of vanishing on a dim or low-gamma display. Still a whisper at 0.22, just a robust one.

ACCURACY — the previous `astroNotes` claimed 'VERIFIED IN BROWSER at 320 / 380 / 440 / 560px' and 'the spine ... measured at exactly 60px at every panel width'. Both were wrong: 320px was broken in two ways, and the spine measures 52px / 60px / 76px depending on width (the 76px because `.term`'s 33rem cap starts centring above 528px). Rewritten with the actual measurements and the tolerances that matter. The spine IS internally exact at each width — that part holds.

REFINEMENT (not a defect) — added a compact vertical scale at ≤360px (`.term` padding-block 1.125rem, `.rows` margin-top 1.125rem, `.foot` margin-top 1rem), since rows roughly double in height when the path drops to its own line. Row padding is deliberately untouched because it is the tap target. This cut `.term` from 475.4px to 451.4px at 320px. Being straight about the residual: that still exceeds a 440px-tall preview panel by ~11px, so the footer sits just below the fold at 320px in the comparison grid. 320px is below the contract's stated 380-560px panel range and is the real-phone case where the page scrolls; within the stated range everything fits (379.9px / 393.5px). I chose not to compress the rhythm further to win 11px in an out-of-range case.

VERIFIED NOT A BUG — the hover/focus rules initially appeared dead: with a programmatic `row.focus()` the element matched `:focus-visible` and got the outline, but the background, marker, label and icon rules all read as resting values. Chrome does not reliably invalidate rules bucketed with `:hover` on programmatic focus. Re-tested with a genuine keyboard Tab through the CDP input domain: focused row resolves to bg `rgba(122,92,255,0.15)`, marker opacity 1, label and icon `rgb(167,139,255)`, plus the 1px dashed outline at -4px offset; unfocused siblings fully reset. Focus is properly distinct from hover. I left this CSS untouched rather than 'fixing' a measurement artifact.

UNITS AND RESOURCES — clean, no changes needed. No vh/vw/dvh/svh/vmin/vmax anywhere. The only `url()` is the inline grain data-URI (verified). No `@import`, no external host, no `<script>`, no `title` attribute, no inline `style` attribute. No `transition: all` — all five transitions name specific properties.

HTML CORRECTNESS — clean, no changes needed; HTML returned unmodified. One real `<h1>`; `<nav aria-label="Profiles and contact">`; six anchors whose hrefs I diffed against the live `src/pages/index.astro` and all six match exactly. `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"` on all five external links and correctly absent on the `mailto:`. All six carry `aria-label`, and every visible label is contained in its accessible name, so WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name holds. Every class in the CSS exists in the markup and every element in the markup is styled. Motion is wrapped in `prefers-reduced-motion` (kills the caret animation and all four transitions), and the caret is pure ornament so nothing is hidden if the animation never runs. Marker-on-hover has no touch equivalent by design — it is `aria-hidden` decoration and the label and path are always visible.

Row heights measure 30.8px (13px rows), 32.3px (14px rows) and 47px (stacked) — all clear the WCAG 2.5.8 24px minimum, though only the stacked case reaches the 44px comfort target. The astroNotes route to ~44px at full-viewport scale via row padding.

Left one upstream asset problem flagged rather than papered over: the Venmo mark in `index.astro` is a serif italic 'V' drawn with SVG `<text>`, not a real logo. It reads visibly foreign beside five solid brand glyphs and its weight depends on a font the SVG cannot guarantee. The 1rem up-scale here compensates for a placeholder; it should be replaced with a real path before launch.

directions.name: Kinetic Minimal
directions.concept: A name, two thin mono lines, a hairline with an accent lead-in, and six lowercase links stacked in one column on a near-flat ground. Nothing decorates it — the craft is in a staggered mask-reveal on load and a four-part hover response that is choreographed rather than merely applied.
directions.rationale: The current page has no identity anchor, so the first move is to put a real 34px name at the top-left and let a two-line mono descriptor carry both halves of the person: the engineering and the running/riding/listening. Everything below it is a single column, which kills the ragged flex-wrap reflow outright — six rows can never break to 2+1 because there is nothing to wrap. Each mark sits in a fixed 1.25rem slot with per-brand optical scaling (GitHub and Spotify pulled down to 17px because a filled disc reads heavy, the solid envelope to 19px so its slab of ink matches that disc rather than exceeding it, Strava's thin chevron pushed to 20px, the typographic Venmo V to 25px so its cap height matches a disc), which is the normalization the current six marks never got. That slot centres with flex, not grid, because a mark deliberately wider than its slot resolves to the start edge of an over-sized grid track instead of its centre. The drop-shadow is gone entirely; the marks are flat and the only light in the page is the accent bloom that appears under your cursor. That bloom, the wiping underline, and the accent mark colour are the first real job the declared --accent has ever had, so the purple favicon finally means something. Both muted greys were re-picked and then verified against both ends of the actual gradient — worst case 5.71:1 light and 6.42:1 dark, versus the 3.12 / 3.42 the site ships today. The mono lowercase labels read as an engineer's list without saying so, and the sans name against them is the whole type system — two roles, no third.
directions.idealTypeface: Söhne (Buch for the name, Kräftig if it wants more weight) paired with Berkeley Mono for the descriptor, labels, and footer. Söhne's Akzidenz-derived flat sides and tight apertures give "Ankur Gupta" a quiet authority system-ui cannot reach, and crucially it holds together at -0.028em tracking where SF Pro starts to collide. Berkeley Mono is the reason to bother: its low-contrast strokes and narrow 600-unit advance make six stacked lowercase labels sit in an even optical rhythm without SF Mono's soft, slightly touristy feel — and at 12px the descriptor stays crisp instead of turning to mush. Both self-host as a single woff2 each (~30KB combined, latin subset). Open substitutes that keep 90% of it: Inter Display SemiBold + IBM Plex Mono.

Ground shadow; only ~3% off bg-1 so the field reads near-flat, not gradient-y. Text is checked against BOTH endpoints, since the gradient means neither one alone is 'the' background
Name and link labels. Worst case 15.45:1 light (on bg-2), 16.00:1 dark (on bg-1)

Radial bloom behind the hovered mark; the only soft light on the page

directions.astroNotes:
Base.astro token surgery, keeping the names where they still mean something: --bg-1/--bg-2 keep their names but take the new near-flat values (#fafafb/#eeeef1 light, #17171b/#0e0e11 dark) and the body gradient re-anchors from `130% 130% at 50% 35%` to `135% 105% at 6% -8%` so the light pools behind the name rather than the middle of nowhere. --fg becomes --ink (#17171a / #f2f2f5). --muted becomes --ink-2 with the fixed values #5c5c66 / #9a9aa6 — this is the one change that must not be skipped, it is the AA failure (the shipped #8a8a90/#6b6b72 are 3.12 / 3.42). --icon becomes --mark (#3f3f47 / #c4c4cc). --icon-hover is deleted; hover is --accent now. --accent stops being decorative and gains a dark variant: #5b3df5 light, #a394ff dark (the shipped #5b3df5 is only ~3.1:1 on the dark ground, so reusing it there would repeat the exact bug being fixed). Add --glow, --sans, --mono, and the five timing tokens. Regenerate public/favicon.svg so its fill is the light --accent verbatim — that relationship is the point. Base.astro currently ships `* { box-sizing: border-box }`, which the preview cannot use; keep it in the real build and the per-element box-sizing declarations here become redundant but harmless. index.astro: the two `
` wrappers disappear entirely and `links` becomes one flat array rendered into a single `
` column, so there is no flex-wrap left to reflow. Each `` gets `class={`link l-${key}`}` for the per-brand optical scaling, an inner `` around the SVG, and a visible `{key}` — which means `aria-label` and `title` both come off (the label is real text now; the title attribute was never doing accessible work anyway). `filter: drop-shadow(...)` is deleted with no replacement. Add the h1 + two-line descriptor above, promote the footer `` to the `

` treatment, and set `--i` via `style={`--i:${i + 4}`}` in the map. Keep `new Date().getFullYear()` rather than the literal 2026 in the preview. Still zero JS: the whole choreography is animation-delay arithmetic. At true full-viewport scale: the stage measure opens from 22rem to 26rem and the whole block stays centred with left-aligned contents (`margin-inline: auto`), so the vertical rhythm grows rather than the line lengths. Name goes to `clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 4rem)` with letter-spacing tightening to -.032em at the top of that ramp; descriptor to .8125rem with letter-spacing .04em and line-height 1.7; labels to 1rem; row padding from .4375rem to .625rem so the six links get a 44px touch target and read as a properly leaded list; rule margins to 2rem/1.5rem and its accent lead-in from 2.5rem to 3.5rem to hold proportion against the longer rule. The mark slot goes to 1.5rem (24px) with all six svg sizes scaled by the same 1.2 factor off the CORRECTED preview values — 1.275rem github, 1.2rem linkedin, 1.425rem email, 1.5rem strava, 1.275rem spotify, 1.875rem venmo. Do not re-derive them; the ratios between the six are the normalization. Note that Venmo is still 30px in a 24px slot, so `.mark` must stay `display: flex` at full scale too — switching it to grid reintroduces the start-edge misalignment. With 44px rows the focus `outline-offset` may rise to 4px but no further: at 5px the 2px stroke reaches the next row's mark again. Body keeps `min-height: 100dvh` with `grid-template-rows: 1fr auto` so the footer pins to the bottom edge instead of floating under the list; the preview's `min-height: 26rem` is replaced by that. The 430px breakpoint stays as written — note it is dead weight in the comparison grid, since media queries key off the viewport and the panel is only ~380-560px inside a much wider window, so the base sizing was verified to read correctly at 380px unaided.
risks: The stagger replays on every single load. It is ~900ms end to end, which is fine the first time and mildly tiresome the twentieth — and there is no zero-JS way to remember that a visitor has already seen it. The honest mitigation is that the total stays under a second and the at-rest page is complete without it; the dishonest one would be adding a sessionStorage flag and giving up the zero-JS property.

Every revealed element uses `animation-fill-mode: both` with a delay, so content is genuinely opacity-0 or translated out of its mask until its delay elapses. prefers-reduced-motion is the escape hatch and it was verified to restore a complete page, but any other path that loads the CSS and then fails to run animations — an aggressive content blocker, a print stylesheet that keeps the animation declarations — leaves rows blank. This is the structural cost of a staggered reveal and it is worth stating out loud rather than discovering.

Two lines of mono descriptor read as confident terseness to engineers and as cryptic to recruiters. 'Runs, rides, records' in particular is a pun that only lands if you already know he is on Strava and Spotify — it is the single most swappable string on the page and should be swapped without hesitation if it does not feel like him.

Lowercase brand labels (github, linkedin, venmo) are a style choice with a shelf life. They read deliberate now; if the taste cycle turns they will read like 2010s startup lowercase. Capitalising all six is a one-line change and costs the design nothing.

The accent lives almost entirely in interaction states, so at rest on a phone the brand purple is a 40px segment of hairline and a 30%-opacity underline. The @media (hover: none) block now gives :active the bloom and the label step as well, but that is still a patch on a real structural asymmetry — this direction is genuinely better on a desktop with a pointer than on a phone.

A left-aligned block centred in a very wide viewport leaves a large quiet right field. That is intentional restraint at 1200px and starts to look like an unfinished layout past ~1800px unless the type ramp actually reaches the 4rem top of its clamp.

The whole page rests on one hover interaction being perfect. If the bloom, the 4px step, and the underline wipe are not timed exactly as specified, this direction has nothing to fall back on — there is no ornament, no texture, and no second idea underneath.

The optical sizing table is six hand-tuned magic numbers tied to six specific SVG viewBoxes. Swap any icon for a differently-proportioned one and its number is silently wrong, with no test to catch it. The Venmo entry is the most fragile: it is a <text> element, so it also depends on Georgia's cap height being available.
qaReport: A. SCOPING — clean, nothing to fix. I parsed all 58 selectors mechanically: every one begins with the literal `SCOPE` except the two `:root[data-theme="dark"|"light"] SCOPE` forms that contract §2 mandates verbatim. No bare `:root`, `html`, `body`, or `*`. All custom properties are declared on `SCOPE`. All three @keyframes are `d5-` prefixed (d5-rise, d5-lift, d5-wipe), so no cross-panel collision. Both theme override blocks present and correctly formed.

B. CONTRAST — no token needed to change, but every ratio the direction QUOTED was wrong, and since the entire rationale is 'we fixed the contrast bug', numbers that do not reproduce are themselves a defect. The author computed against one gradient endpoint only; the true worst case is the other one. Recomputed all pairs against BOTH bg-1 and bg-2 with the real relative-luminance formula: --ink 15.45 light / 16.00 dark (claimed 15.9 / 17.3); --ink-2 5.71 light / 6.42 dark (claimed 5.86 / 6.95); --mark 9.01 light (claimed 9.2); --accent 5.29 light / 7.01 dark (claimed 5.6 / 7.5). All still clear AA, so the palette is untouched and only the reported figures are corrected in the palette roles.

B (cont). --rule is 1.24:1 light / 1.19:1 dark, below the 3:1 UI-component floor. Reported explicitly rather than left silent: this is an intentional 1.4.11 exemption, not a miss. The rule is an `aria-hidden` span that conveys no information and is not a control. Its role string now says so, so nobody 'fixes' it later and wrecks the near-flat ground.

C. UNITS AND RESOURCES — clean, nothing to fix. Grepped the CSS: zero vh/vw/dvh/svh/lvh/vmin/vmax, zero url() pointing at a host, no @import, no @font-face, no <script>, no `transition: all`. Grepped the HTML: no `title` attribute anywhere, and the only inline styles are the eleven `--i:N` custom properties used for the stagger.

Measured offset of the Venmo mark's centre from its slot's centre was dx +2.5px, dy +2.5px, so the one mark the direction deliberately over-sizes was the one mark pushed off the shared left edge and down out of the row's optical centre — destroying exactly the alignment the fixed slot exists to guarantee. Switched `.mark` to `display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center`, which overflows symmetrically. Re-measured: dx 0, dy 0.

D1 (cont). That fix needed a second half the author could not have known about: flex items default to `flex-shrink: 1`, so the 25px Venmo SVG would have been squeezed back to 20px and the optical scaling silently reverted. Added `flex: none` to `SCOPE .mark svg`; confirmed the rendered width stays 25px.

D2. REAL BUG, measured — the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block set `.label::after { opacity: 0 }` at the same specificity as, and later in source than, the `@media (hover: none)` block's `{ opacity: .3 }`. On a touch device with reduced motion enabled, the computed opacity resolved to 0, silently deleting the resting-underline affordance that the (hover: none) block exists solely to provide — the worst kind of accessibility bug, where turning one a11y setting on removes another. Verified 0 before / 0.3 after by forcing both media conditions true and reading getComputedStyle on the pseudo-element. Fixed by moving the cross-fade rules into `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and (hover: hover)`.

D3. Touch parity — `:focus-visible` did nothing to the underline on a hover:none device (the base focus rule only sets `transform: scaleX(1)`, which is already the resting value there, so a keyboard user on a tablet got the ring and nothing else). Added `:focus-visible` alongside `:active` in the hover:none opacity rule. Separately, touch got only 2 of the advertised 4 hover parts; added `:active` bloom and `:active` label step so the choreography survives, with both neutralised again under reduced motion.

E1. REAL DEFECT, measured — `outline-offset: 6px` on flush 32px rows put the focus ring's outer edge at exactly the next row's icon top edge: 0.0px clearance, and 0.3px of overlap into the next label's box. A ring that grazes the neighbouring content is a ring that will cross it on any device whose font metrics or DPR round differently. Fixed by taking `.link` padding from .375rem to .4375rem (34px rows) and `outline-offset` from 6px to 3px; re-measured clearance is 4.0px. Bonus: 34px rows clear WCAG 2.5.8 target size (24x24) with room, where 32px was already fine but tighter.

E2. Choreography contradicted the concept — the rule is described as an accent 'lead-in', but at 700ms starting on step 3 it finished at 872ms, AFTER five of the six links had already landed, so it read as the slowest thing on the page rather than the thing leading. Extracted it to a `--rule-dur: 620ms` token and trimmed `--step` from 44ms to 40ms. The rule now completes at 780ms, before the last link at 860ms, and the total drops from ~940ms to ~900ms. `--dur` and `--ease` are untouched.

E3. Optical normalization contradicted its own stated principle — the email envelope was the only mark left at the full 1.25rem slot size, giving a 20x15px solid slab of ~255px^2 of ink versus the GitHub disc's ~227px^2 at 17px. The direction explicitly pulls discs DOWN because filled shapes read heavy, then left the heaviest shape on the page at full size. Reduced to 1.1875rem (19px, ~230px^2), which matches the disc it was supposed to be normalised against. This is the only size in the table I changed.

E4. `min-height: 27rem` (432px) against a stated ~440px panel left 8px of headroom. Measured content stack is 411px. Lowered to 26rem (416px) so a slightly shorter host panel can never force a scrollbar, while still filling a 440px one. Verified scrollHeight === clientHeight at 380x440, 420x440, and 560x440.

E5. Fragility, not yet a bug — `SCOPE .links` relied on `width: fit-content` on the children alone to defeat the default `align-items: stretch` of a column flex container; removing that one declaration would have silently given every row full width and a full-width focus ring. Added `align-items: flex-start`. Likewise added `box-sizing: border-box` to `.link`, the only remaining element with both padding and a width, since the `*` selector is banned and the host page's reset is unknown. I checked every other element and confirmed none of them depends on box-sizing.

E6. Verified, no change needed — the mask-reveal arithmetic is actually correct. At line-height 1.05 with .14em padding-bottom the name's descenders land at 36.9px inside a 40.5px clip box (not clipped at rest), and the 132% travel (1.386em) exceeds the 1.19em clip height so the text is fully hidden before it rises. Same holds for the descriptor at line-height 1.55 with .16em. The extra ~3px of leading the two role masks introduce between the descriptor's lines is consistent between them, so the rhythm is even; I left it.

E7. Verified, no change needed — forced `animation: none` and confirmed every element resolves to opacity 1 / transform none, `.mark` transition reduces to `color` only, and the bloom keeps `transform: scale(1)` while cross-fading opacity. The claim that killing animation restores a complete legible page holds. Reduced motion is the only guaranteed path to that state, which is now stated as a risk rather than left implicit.

D/E. Verified, no change needed — HTML was already correct and I returned it structurally unchanged. All six hrefs cross-checked byte-for-byte against src/pages/index.astro; all five external links carry target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" and the mailto carries neither; real <h1> for the name; <nav aria-label="Profiles and contact">; all six marks aria-hidden with real visible text labels, so no aria-label is needed and none is missing; :focus-visible present and visually distinct from hover (it adds the ring hover never shows). Measured text widths at the narrowest 380px panel — name 183.5px, longest descriptor line 186.6px, footer 135px, all inside a 324px stage — so nothing wraps or overflows without the 430px breakpoint, which cannot fire in the comparison grid anyway.
