directions.name: Depth and Grain
directions.concept: A flat near-black ground, one broad accent bloom sited behind the identity as a single light source, and a fine additive grain laid over everything including the tiles. The six mismatched marks are put on one optical grid inside frosted hairline tiles, each glyph individually sized to match apparent weight rather than box.
directions.rationale: The six links have no shared visual system, so the fix is to build one: a fixed 28px glyph cell inside an identical tile, with per-mark optical sizing (Strava's thin chevrons at 1.18rem rendering 18.9px, GitHub's filled disc at 0.98rem rendering 15.7px) so a filled circle and a typographic V finally read at the same weight. A 2x3 grid replaces two wrapping flex rows, so there is no ragged intermediate reflow at any width — 6 divides evenly by 2, and the two columns hold down to a 142px tile with no label wrapping and no sub-label truncation. Left-aligned name, tagline and link grid reads as an actual page rather than a centered badge wall, which is what made the original feel unfinished. The tagline does triple duty in one line: engineering, endurance sport, music. And the declared-but-unused #5b3df5 finally earns the favicon: it is the bloom, the hover hairline and glow, the mark dot, and the focus ring — four coherent uses, all traceable to one light source.
directions.idealTypeface: Inter Display (or Inter v4 with `opsz`), self-hosted woff2, weights 400/500/600 plus a mono for the wordmark — Berkeley Mono if licensed, otherwise JetBrains Mono. system-ui is doing an acceptable job here because SF Pro is genuinely good: I confirmed the 550 on the tile labels computes to a real 550 on macOS. But it collapses on Windows to Segoe UI, which is not variable, so that 550 snaps to 600, and Segoe's looser default tracking costs the name its density on half the audience. Inter Display buys a consistent tight-tracked 600 from 26 to 56px on every platform, a real 550 via variable weight, and tabular-safe small text for the 11px sub-labels. The mono matters more than it looks: "goobta.io" set in a deliberate mono is the one place the page says "engineer" without saying it.
directions.proposedTagline: Software and AI engineering. Long rides, loud records.

palette.role: Flat deep ground. Intentionally flat — the bloom and grain do all tonal modulation. Set below #0a0a0d because the additive grain lifts the composited average: measured +4.7/255 mean, so the field reads ~#0e0e11 and peaks near #121215.

The favicon purple, finally used. Decorative only — measured 1.71:1 on a tile bed and 3.25:1 on the bare ground, so it is never applied to text. Drives the bloom, hover hairline, hover glow, dot halo.

Accent lightened until it is safe as a visible graphic: the 5px mark dot and the 2px focus ring. Worst case 4.84:1 against the field just outside a tile and 4.28:1 against the tile bed itself — both past the 3:1 needed for non-text UI, on both sides of the 3px outline offset.
Name, tile labels, hovered glyph. 8.94:1 at the synthetic worst case (bloom core, saturated backdrop, hovered tile bed, grain peak); 14.35:1 where the grid actually sits.
Tagline, resting glyph, hovered sub-label. 4.98:1 worst case on a hovered tile, 6.14:1 for the tagline over the bloom.

Wordmark, resting tile sub-labels, footer. 4.64:1 at the synthetic ceiling and 6.83:1 at the tiles' real position; replaces --muted, which failed at 3.42:1. Deliberately only three steps off --ink-2 — that gap is the sub-label's hover lift, so it cannot be raised for margin without erasing the state change.
The 1px tile border. 11%, not 9% — at 9% the tiles dissolved in the dark lower-right where the bloom does not reach.
Tile body. Translucent so backdrop-filter has something to sample where the bloom crosses a tile.
Hovered/focused tile body. A 3-point lift, cross-faded, never a translate.
inset 0 1px 0 top-edge highlight. Sits inside the border, so tile top edges get a border-then-lip double edge consistent with light arriving from upper left.
Hover state of the lip — the tile appears to tilt into the light rather than move.

The tile's ambient contact shadow, tokenised because it now appears in three shadow lists (rest, hover, coarse-pointer reset). Single-sourcing it is what stops a future editor from drifting one copy and inventing a second glow.

directions.astroNotes:
MAPPING ONTO Base.astro — this direction replaces the token block rather than extending it. --bg-1/--bg-2 and the body radial-gradient go away entirely: the ground is flat and the bloom is a separate element, which is the whole point of the layering. Keep --accent: #5b3df5 verbatim (it is the favicon) and add --accent-lift: #a394ff plus --drop. --fg -> --ink, --icon -> --ink-2. Delete --muted: it fails AA in both themes and every one of its uses is now --ink-3. Drop `color-scheme: light dark` and set `color-scheme: dark` so form controls and scrollbars match; add `<meta name="theme-color" content="#09090c">`. On SCOPE-as-body: keep display:flex/column, position:relative, isolation:isolate, and DROP overflow:hidden — the bloom is inset:0 so nothing bleeds, and overflow:hidden on body kills scroll anchoring. The existing global `* { box-sizing: border-box }` already covers the border-box declarations. .bloom and .grain become the first and last children of body, outside <main>; the reveal --i values stay as literal inline custom props in the template — keep them, but note the CSS now reads var(--i, 0), so a forgotten one degrades to a 90ms delay instead of firing at 0s with the rest. Keep role="list" on the <ul>: list-style:none strips the list role in Safari/VoiceOver, and without it the six links stop announcing as a set. Footer year goes back to {new Date().getFullYear()}.

HEIGHT AND CENTERING — use `min-height: 100dvh`, never `height`. With min-height, tall content grows the page and nothing is lost; with a fixed height, `justify-content: center` on an overflowing column puts the top of the composition outside the scrollable area where it cannot be reached. That is also why the preview keeps overflow:hidden and the page must not. For the optical lift, use asymmetric block padding (e.g. padding-block: 4vh 6vh in page terms) rather than translateY(-2%) — a transform moves painted content without moving the scroll box, so it reintroduces the same unreachable-overflow failure on a short viewport.

AT TRUE FULL-VIEWPORT SCALE — the panel is a 380-560px box, so the type ramp is deliberately compressed and must open up. .name: clamp(2.5rem, 1.4rem + 5cqw, 3.5rem) with the static fallback raised to 2.75rem, and letter-spacing tightening to -0.03em as it grows (large display sizes need less tracking, not the same). .lede: 1.0625rem/1.6, max-width 34ch. Tile .label 0.9375rem, .sub 0.8125rem, glyph cell 2.25rem with every --g scaled by ~1.25 — the six optical ratios are the deliverable, not the absolute sizes, so scale them together and do not re-guess them. Tile padding to 0.875rem/1rem, radius 14px, grid gap 0.75rem. The .nav max-width:34rem cap already prevents the two columns from sprawling on a 27-inch display; the whole composition sits in a ~34rem column, left-aligned.

THE CONTAINER QUERY MUST MOVE AT PAGE SCALE. Measured in the panel: the stage content box is 272px (17.0rem) at 320px, 328px at 375px, 341px at 390px, because the padding clamp bottoms out at 1.5rem below a 384px viewport. So 17.5rem drops to one column at a 320px phone and nowhere else — correct for the preview, where the tiles are 13px/11px and two 142px columns still measure clean. With the ~1.25x page ramp, a 375-390px phone would run two 158px columns whose text cell is 82px against a 78px "work history", i.e. one character from truncating. On the real page raise the query to `@container (max-width: 23rem)` so every phone gets one column and the desktop keeps 2x3. Do not simply reuse 17.5rem there. Two build details: the grain data-URI must stay single-quoted internally with %23 for the two `#` characters or Astro's CSS minifier will truncate it at the fragment, and Astro scoped styles will not reach the injected SVGs, so `.glyph svg` needs :global() (or set:html the icons and keep that rule in the is:global block). Bloom percentages are resolution-independent so the 8-stop falloff holds at any size; the grain's 128px tile is fixed in CSS px, which is correct — grain should be a constant perceptual size. Page stays zero-JS.
risks: Committed dark is a real bet. The host page stamps data-theme and I emit no light tokens, so a viewer who deliberately flips to light gets the dark card anyway and may read it as broken rather than intentional. I chose this because a frosted tile with a top-edge highlight and an additive grain is a dark-UI idiom — the light-mode translation would be a different design wearing this one's name — but if the user wants a working light mode, this is the direction that has to change most.

This is the most-imitated look on the internet right now. The bloom-plus-grain-plus-frosted-tile vocabulary reads as 2023-2026 SaaS, and it will date as a period style the way skeuomorphic gradients and long shadows did. The discipline (one bloom, one grain, one accent, no crude translate) is what separates it from the pastiche, and that discipline is exactly what a future editor is most likely to erode by adding a second glow. The --drop token exists partly to make that harder.

mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter is load-bearing for the grain. Measured on this ground it contributes +4.7/255 on average and +9.4/255 at peaks; overlay and soft-light collapse to ~0.4/255 and do literally nothing, so the usual copy-pasted grain recipe is invisible here. plus-lighter degrades to normal compositing, within 1/255 on a dark field, so the fallback is safe. But the grain silently stops mattering if the ground is ever lightened, and every contrast figure in the palette is computed with the grain peak added — anyone raising --ground must re-derive both.

The tile secondary labels ("the code", "work history") are voice, and voice is the most personal thing here. They read as considered to me and twee to someone else, and they are the first thing I would expect the user to rewrite. They are also the reason the tiles can be 2-up at 380px — the strings are capped near 12 characters and will ellipsis rather than wrap if lengthened.

Six backdrop-filter tiles each get their own compositor layer. It is fine on this page but it is not free, and on a low-end Android the blur may quietly not render — the tiles still read correctly from fill plus hairline plus lip, so this fails soft, but the frosted quality is the part that would be lost.

The bloom sits top-left and the lower-right of the frame stays near-black. I read that as depth and a believable light source; it can also read as an empty half, and at 440px tall the band below the footer is the emptiest part of the composition. Nudging the bloom center down to ~18% 6% fills the field more but weakens the off-frame light-source illusion that justifies the tiles' top-edge highlight, so the two are coupled and cannot be tuned independently.

The reveal masks each element, and an active mask clips outer box-shadow and outline. This is handled — fill-mode is backwards only, so the mask is gone at rest, and :focus-visible sets animation:none so a tile focused during the first second snaps to an unclipped ring — but it is a non-obvious coupling. Moving the mask longhands out of the keyframes onto the elements, which looks like a tidy-up, would permanently clip every tile's contact shadow and every focus ring.
qaReport: SCOPING: clean, verified mechanically rather than by eye. Parsed all 46 selector groups — every one begins with the literal SCOPE token, no :root/html/body/* anywhere, all custom properties declared on SCOPE, both keyframe names prefixed (d3-wipe, d3-bloom), and the @media/@container blocks wrap SCOPE-prefixed selectors. commitsToSingleTheme is true, so the single token set with no light/dark override blocks is contract-legal. Nothing to fix here.

UNITS AND RESOURCES: clean. No vh/vw/dvh/svh (only %, rem, px, ch, cqw and clamp). The one url() is the inline grain data-URI, and the url(%23g) inside it is a same-document filter reference, not a network request. No <script>, no title attribute, and the only inline styles are the nine --i custom properties used for the stagger.

CONTRAST: recomputed every text pair with the real relative-luminance formula against composited backgrounds, not against the flat token — bloom over ground, then the tile's own saturate(135%) backdrop filter, then the translucent fill, then the additive grain at its measured peak. All 12 pairs pass. The palette's originally stated figures were optimistic and unsourced (it claimed --ink 9.88, --ink-2 5.50, --ink-3 5.11, --accent-lift 4.71); every role string now carries the number I actually computed, plus the realistic figure at the element's true position in the frame.

CONTRAST, worst pair: --ink-3 sub-labels at 4.64:1 against a synthetic ceiling (34% bloom directly under a hovered tile, saturated, at the grain peak). That ceiling is unreachable — the bloom's 34% stop is at 14%/-8%, above the frame, and by the vertical band where the grid sits the bloom has fallen to ~5%, which measures 6.83:1. I deliberately did NOT raise --ink-3: it is only three steps off --ink-2, and that gap IS the sub-label's hover lift, so buying margin there would erase a state change to fix a number that already passes.

GRAIN: measured instead of asserted. Rasterised the data-URI off-screen — mean alpha 0.5 as intended, mean effective value 93/255 — so at opacity 0.05 under plus-lighter it adds +4.7/255 mean and +9.4/255 peak. The author's claim that the composited average lands near #0d0d10 is right (I get ~#0e0e11, peaking #121215). I also went looking for the bug I expected here, a seam from stitchTiles running against the filter region's default 10% bleed, and it is not present: cross-tile column delta 28.4 vs 31.7 for an interior pair, i.e. seamless. Recorded both measurements in the CSS comment so nobody 'fixes' a working filter.

FIXED — dead fluid type. clamp(1.625rem, 6.6cqw, 2.125rem) sat on its 26px floor from 280px all the way to 440px and only moved at 560px, so across most of the stated 380-560px range the name did not respond to width at all. Re-derived as clamp(1.625rem, 0.85rem + 4.2cqw, 2.125rem); measured 26 / 27.5 / 29.8 / 34px at 320 / 380 / 440 / 560. Floor and ceiling unchanged, so neither extreme of the design moves.

FIXED — no static font-size fallback on the name. With the whole declaration resting on a container unit, an engine without cqw dropped it and the h1 fell back to whatever the host comparison page gives an h1. Added font-size: 1.75rem ahead of the clamp.

FIXED — Safari list semantics. list-style: none on the <ul> strips the list role in Safari/VoiceOver, so the six links stopped announcing as 'list, 6 items'. Added role="list". Confirmed the ul had no role and computed list-style-type: none.

FIXED — stagger custom property had no fallback. Measured it: a tile with no --i computed animation-delay: 0s, not 90ms, because calc(90ms + var(--i) * 48ms) goes invalid at computed-value time and resets to initial. Now var(--i, 0). This matters because astroNotes hands those nine values to a template by hand.

FIXED — sticky hover on touch. Five of the six tiles open a new tab, so the tapped tile is still on screen when the user comes back, holding the accent border and the glow indefinitely. Added an @media (hover: none) reset of exactly the three hover rules, leaving :focus-visible untouched so keyboard focus still lifts. To avoid a second copy of the shadow stack drifting from the first, I tokenised the shared ambient shadow as --drop; it now appears once and is referenced three times.

FIXED — dead transition. The tile's transition list included color, but nothing renders the tile's own color: .label, .sub and .glyph each set their own. Removed color from the list. The color declaration itself stays as a sane inherited default.

FIXED — vertical rhythm. 22px (.head margin-bottom), 10px (.lede margin-top) and 7px (.mark gap) were the only three values off the 4px step everything else uses (12 / 8 / 20). Now 24 / 12 / 8. The gap change also corrects an optical error: the dot's 3px halo ate the 7px flex gap down to a 4px visible gap between glow and the 'g' of goobta.io, measured; it is 5px now.

FIXED — boundary-critical container query. The stage's content box is exactly 272px = 17.000rem at a 320px panel, because the padding clamp bottoms out at 1.5rem below 384px. max-width: 17rem therefore fired precisely on the boundary, where a scrollbar or a half-pixel flips the whole layout. Moved to 17.5rem: behaviourally identical (the next measured step up is 18.25rem at 340px) and no longer knife-edge. Verified two columns hold down to a 142px tile with zero label wraps and zero sub-label ellipsis at every width from 280 to 560px.

REPORTED, NOT FIXED — one-column mode does not fit the preview harness. Below the query threshold the six-row stack measures 496px, which a 440px panel with overflow:hidden clips by ~76px with no way to scroll to it. That only happens at a panel of 320px or less, outside the contract's 380-560px range; in range the content is 325-332px tall in 440px with symmetric 57-60px gaps. It is not a page bug either, because the body uses min-height, so the page grows rather than clipping — but astroNotes now states that explicitly, since changing min-height to height would convert justify-content:center into unreachable top overflow.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED — clamping .label to one line with an ellipsis to match .sub. Measured no label wrapping at any width from 280 to 560px, and if one ever did, wrapping the link's own name is a better failure than truncating it. The sub-labels are throwaway voice, so ellipsis belongs there and only there. Left a comment saying so.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED — retuning the six --g optical sizes. Rendered glyph widths measure 15.7 / 15.4 / 16.3 / 18.9 / 16.3 / 19.8px; inspected at 2.6x I read LinkedIn's block as marginally the heaviest mass and Strava's chevron as marginally the lightest, so I would personally go 0.94rem and 1.20rem. That is a ±2% disagreement with the author's own stated deliverable, not a defect, so it stays as authored.

MOTION, verified: fill-mode is backwards only, so if the animation never runs nothing is left at opacity 0 or masked — content is never animation-blocked. prefers-reduced-motion kills all five animations, the bloom transform and the three transitions. Total stagger measured at 1034ms (last tile delay 474ms plus 560ms duration), which does not drag. The documented mask/box-shadow coupling is intact, and I left the mask longhands inside the keyframes rather than hoisting them onto the elements, because hoisting is what would permanently clip the contact shadows and focus rings.

FOCUS, verified by rendering the state rather than reading the CSS: the 2px accent-lift ring at 3px offset reads clearly as focus and is distinct from hover, which has no ring at all. It also clears the 3:1 non-text requirement on both sides of the offset gap — 4.84:1 against the field outside the tile and 4.28:1 against the tile bed. No change.

ENGINE SUPPORT, verified in the target browser: plus-lighter, color-mix(in oklab), backdrop-filter, container-type, cqw and text-wrap:balance all supported, backdrop-filter computing as blur(6px) saturate(1.35), and font-weight 550 computing as a real 550. I also checked whether the color-mix tokens need an @supports fallback and concluded they do not: the design already requires container units, and no shipping engine has container queries without color-mix, so a fallback would be dead code.
